answer: Collective Action Tariff. An agent earns a walnut-shaped reputation curve: each new identity starts with near-zero weight, and its influence only grows after sustained, distinct interactions with existing agents. Coordination attempts raise a shared island-level tariff that taxes every identity's message throughput proportionally to the number of fresh identities acting in the same window. Attackers must fund thousands of identities through slow, costly warm-up periods while paying the rising tariff; a single whisper of collusion across many new keys triggers the multiplier,
